title.narrative: Digitalisation for Growth, Integrity & Transparency Project (UK DIGIT)

description.narrative: The Digitalisation for Growth, Integrity, and Transparency (UK DIGIT) Project aims to strengthen trust between the people of Ukraine and the state by fighting corruption, improving service delivery, and increasing domestic revenues while creating a modern, two-way partnership that feeds lessons from Ukrainian innovation back to the UK. The Project will strengthen Ukraine today while creating long-term, shared capability in both countries.

UK DIGIT has three core objectives: (1) Build more responsive, transparent, and effective public services; (2) Support economic recovery and mobilise domestic revenue; (3) Leverage mutual opportunities for the UK and Ukraine through partnership on innovation

UK DIGIT is funded by the United Kingdom's Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO). It is implemented by a consortium led by Eurasia Foundation (EF) in collaboration with the Better Regulation Delivery Office (BRDO) and East Europe Foundation (EEF).
UK DIGIT's key beneficiaries include Ukraine's Ministry of Digital Transformation (MDT), Ministry of Economy and Environment (MoEE), Ministry for Recovery, Infrastructure and Transport (MRIT), National Agency on Corruption Prevention (NACP); and others.
EF and its partners have extensive expertise in digital transformation, deregulation, public procurement integrity, and anti-corruption policy development. Together, they work to develop and implement long-term sustainable digital governance strategies that align with Ukraine’s European integration and modernisation agenda.

title.narrative: Outcome 3. UK–Ukraine innovation cooperation is structured and results-oriented across priority innovation tracks (e.g., TechBridge delivery, WINWIN high-tech priorities, venture ecosystem mechanisms)
Indicator 3.2.4. Ukraine’s global country rank in StartupBlink Global Startup Ecosystem Index

comment.narrative: 42nd place in 2025.
41st place.

Ukraine ranked 43rd place in the global rankings in the StartupBlink Global Startup Ecosystem Index, below the target of 41st place, and a decline of 1 place from the baseline of 42nd place in 2025. This reflects the continued impact of the full-scale war, including lower investment and the continued relocation of startups and skilled talent outside of Ukraine. At the same time, UK DIGIT is contributing to strengthening Ukraine's innovation ecosystem through initiatives such as the WINWIN Strategy, Diia.City Invest Fund, and MedTech Sandbox. As these interventions take time to deliver results, and their impact is expected to be reflected in the future StartupBlink ranking.
